prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web product UI concept, landscape 1536x1024
Primary request: Design a structure-led Baseball Dashboard dedicated one-game Player Props page for CIN at SF. This is a separate page, not a sidebar. Carry over the visual character of Reference Image 1—browser/app chrome, palette, typography, compact scorecard components—but do not copy its split-pane content or layout.
Input images: Reference Image 1 is visual style and incumbent-product reference only; it is not an edit target and its composition must not be retained.
Scene/backdrop: Full-width dark baseball analytics application inside restrained browser chrome. At top, retain a compact dark-green app header labeled "BASEBALL DASHBOARD", then a compact game identity row with breadcrumb "ALL GAMES / CIN @ SF", status "MON · 6:45 PM PDT", Cincinnati Reds versus San Francisco Giants, Oracle Park, and a small navigation tab row with "OVERVIEW", "PLAYER PROPS" active, and "BEST LEANS".
Subject: A dedicated single-game Player Props decision workspace. Directly below game identity, create a sticky full-width scoring strip titled "CUMULATIVE SCORE WEIGHTS". It contains three precise horizontal sliders labeled "MODEL CONFIDENCE", "STATISTICAL EDGE", and "MARKET VALUE"; show weights 40%, 35%, and 25%, a clear "100% TOTAL" validation, a compact "RESET" control, and formula cue "SCORE = CONFIDENCE × 40% + EDGE × 35% + VALUE × 25%". Beneath, the main content is four parallel horizontal market lanes / columns titled "PITCHER STRIKEOUTS", "OUTS RECORDED", "HITS", and "TOTAL BASES", each with a small prop count and ranked like-for-like cards stacked vertically.
Card details: Every ranked card must clearly show rank, small circular player headshot, player name and team mark, lean direction as OVER or UNDER, line, American odds, three factor mini-bars with numeric values, a large cumulative score out of 100, and a compact evidence disclosure row such as "LAST 30", "MATCHUP", "PRICE" with a chevron. Use realistic visible examples: Chase Burns — OVER 6.5 strikeouts +100, score 82; Chase Burns — UNDER 17.5 outs -128, score 67; Jung Hoo Lee — OVER 0.5 hits -179, score 88; Rafael Devers — OVER 0.5 hits -120, score 79; Bryce Eldridge — OVER 1.5 total bases +115, score 74. Add secondary cards as needed while keeping content dense and legible. Show strongest score with a thin gold left rule and "TOP LEAN", not sportsbook bet-slip styling.
Style/medium: Production-grade high-fidelity web UI screenshot, dense highly scannable Operate-mode analytics dashboard. IBM Plex Sans / Barlow Condensed scorecard feel, uppercase condensed labels, tabular numerals, crisp realistic interface rendering.
Composition/framing: Full viewport, 1536x1024 landscape. Strong top-to-bottom hierarchy: app header, compact game context, sticky scoring controls, then four evenly proportioned market lanes across the full content width. Avoid a right sidebar. Align cards rigorously in a comparison grid. Generous enough gutters for scanability, but no wasteful hero area.
Color palette: preserve exactly the incumbent family: near-black #101613 canvas, flat deep-green panels #18211c, off-white #e8eae6 type, gold #e5b54e ticks and strongest-score accents, coral #e07b6c for over/positive lean, dusty blue #82aecf for under/alternate values. Muted gray-green secondary text and subtle hairline borders.
Materials/textures: flat restrained panels, 1px hairlines, small inset card surfaces, squared corners with only slight radius, no shadows except barely perceptible separation.
Text (verbatim where specified): "BASEBALL DASHBOARD"; "ALL GAMES / CIN @ SF"; "PLAYER PROPS"; "BEST LEANS"; "CUMULATIVE SCORE WEIGHTS"; "MODEL CONFIDENCE"; "STATISTICAL EDGE"; "MARKET VALUE"; "40%"; "35%"; "25%"; "100% TOTAL"; "RESET"; "SCORE = CONFIDENCE × 40% + EDGE × 35% + VALUE × 25%"; "PITCHER STRIKEOUTS"; "OUTS RECORDED"; "HITS"; "TOTAL BASES"; "TOP LEAN".
Constraints: Information architecture and layout matter more than decorative styling. All four lanes and scoring controls must be visible in one desktop viewport. Cards must be comparable at a glance. Use accessible contrast, tabular numerals, credible baseball data density, small gold section ticks, subtle evidence disclosure affordances. Preserve exact names and core numbers requested above. No gradients.
Avoid: split-pane layout, sidebar player props, sportsbook bet-slip chrome, wager buttons, casino motifs, glossy effects, glassmorphism, neon, gradients, giant title, decorative hero, oversized cards, excessive pills, floating rounded containers, charts without labels, illegible microtext, fake performance claims, logos copied inaccurately, watermarks.
